title: Heart Of Titanium Glass
author: William Saville
content:
Stiletto heels on brick,
Stepping on broken glass,
Shards reflect your face.
Silicone fake and nose upturned.
Looking down at me.
Cold glass sharp heart like you,
Reflections show outside beauty but that's not what I see.
Wear that cross and walk by,
Wallets filled,
Heart empty Soul gone But does your spirit remain?
Yes,
You use it to point out my flaws.
But your god teaches you kindness.
To remove the log in your own eye,
Before pointing at the dust in mine.
Fly time,
Grasping angel wings,
I breathe in and out
Try not to break as you try to take away all I have left.
My dignity.
Fall fast,
Or drown,
Whichever one you prefer,
Either I am falling or drowning,
And you are blind to what is in front of you.
I feel sorry for you.
Wrapped in your own life,
Only your voice matters,
I bite my tongue and bleed,
Try not to break down as you smile at me so falsely.
You tell me you will pray for me, as you hold my hand stiffly,
Yank your hand away once it's done, grab cross and off you run,
Hypocrite and false preacher,
I will say.
You should pray for yourself not for me.
